text: The authors state (informally, with formal versions in Appendix B) that Theorems 4.1 and 4.2 hold exactly with (c, q, eta)-expansion instead of (c, q)-expansion and R_eta(f) instead of R(f), giving guarantees for average-case-robust classifiers under a robust-expansion assumption on the data distribution. They argue this generalization is important because adversarial training and adversarial robustness are not required for weak-to-strong generalization to occur empirically.
title: Theorem 4.3: bounds extend to average-case-robust students under robust expansion
